summary.title: 68 Resources To Help You To Create Programming Languages
summary.one_liner: A curated, annotated list of articles, books, tutorials and tools for designing a programming language, writing its parser, and implementing it as a compiler or interpreter.
takeaways: Language creation splits into three stages: design, parsing (lexer and parser producing an AST), and execution (compiler or interpreter).
Books such as Types and Programming Languages and Practical Foundations for Programming Languages cover the theory behind language design and type systems.
Classic parser tools are Flex, Bison/Yacc and ANTLR, each with tutorials and books recommended in the list.
For execution, the page points to LLVM tutorials, the Dragon and Tiger compiler books, and interpreter walkthroughs in Python, JavaScript, Go and C#.
Language workbenches such as Racket, Xtext and JetBrains MPS cover the whole process, from parsing to IDE support.
summary.summary: This page is a resource guide organized around the three stages of building a programming language: design, parsing, and execution, with a general section for end-to-end tools. Each entry is a short annotation saying what the resource covers, its level, and whether it is dated or theory-heavy. Resources include articles, PDF papers, books, video tutorials, and tools such as LLVM, ANTLR, Xtext, JetBrains MPS and Racket. The author's comments help readers choose between theoretical and pragmatic material.
